title: Cones and countable direct sums of K-flat complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. If $(K_n^\bullet)_{n\in\mathbf N}$ is a countable family of K-flat complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex], then $\bigoplus_n K_n^\bullet$ is K-flat, and the mapping cone of every morphism of K-flat complexes is K-flat.

source.place: Lemma 06YS (closure of K-flat complexes under cones and direct sums)

proof.text: For every acyclic test complex A, install the monoidal closed structure from [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] and the Grothendieck abelian structure from [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The proved source-library BifunctorColimits instances show that the functor Tot(A tensor -) preserves countable coproducts, giving PreservesCoproduct.iso. Each Tot(A tensor K_n) is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The proved private Lean helper acyclic_coproduct_nat applies exactness of coproducts (AB4, obtained from the Grothendieck property by filtered colimits of finite sums): each zero-to-summand map is a quasi-isomorphism by quasiIsoAt_iff_exactAt, the coproduct map is a quasi-isomorphism by HomologicalComplex.isStableUnderCoproducts_quasiIso, and its source is zero by the coproduct universal property. Thus the sum of the tensor complexes is acyclic. Transfer ExactAt in each degree along the inverse tensor/coproduct comparison. This proves K-flatness of the countable sum.

source.place: Lemma 06YR, closure under filtered colimits, applied to finite partial coproducts

proof.text: For a map f of K-flat complexes, unfold [def-pc-kflat-complex] and test against an arbitrary acyclic complex A. The two hypotheses make Tot(A tensor K1) and Tot(A tensor K2) acyclic. Apply the first two-to-third implication in SheafOfModules.tensor_mappingCone_two_out_of_three [lem-pc-kflat-tensor-cone-two-out-of-three] to conclude that Tot(A tensor mappingCone(f)) is acyclic; the mapping cone is the existing cone construction [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This is precisely IsKFlat of the mapping cone.
